issues.title: Missing sampling contract in the Wendland total-error theorem

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and choose $m_j = m \in \bN$ i.i.d. samples from every $\rho_{x_j}$, $j = 1, \dots, d$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states only kernel-space and Koopman-operator hypotheses before using m in its probability bound. The estimator was previously defined with potentially unequal counts m_j, whereas thm:mc_error1, invoked by the proof, explicitly assumes m_j=m i.i.d. samples at every design point. That assumption occurs inside another theorem and is not inherited by this separate result, so the invocation and the printed occurrence of m are unjustified as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The specialized Wendland total-error theorem is not a closed probabilistic assertion and its proof establishes the displayed confidence bound only after a sample-count convention is supplied. The general total-error and Monte Carlo theorems remain unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to thm:total_err_wendland and its restatement the premise that, for each design point x_j, the matrix K_{X,Y}^{MC} is formed from m_j=m i.i.d. draws from rho_{x_j}. This defines m and makes thm:mc_error1 directly applicable without changing the displayed error or confidence bounds.
issues.why_classification: A probabilistic hypothesis required by the proof is genuinely absent, so this is not merely transcriptional. The equal-count i.i.d. sampling contract is nevertheless a short, routine, source-supported local qualification that preserves the estimator, conclusion, rate, confidence guarantee, and entire affected chain.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Furthermore, for~$\mathcal{X} = \{x_1,\ldots,x_d\} \subset \Omega$, let $m_j = m \in \bN$ i.i.d.\ samples from every $\rho_{x_j}$, $j \in \{1, \dots, d\}$, be given.

issues.title: Incorrect left factor in the numerical regularized approximant
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that its displayed expression is the regularized approximant defined in eq:regularized_mcemdmd. The old labeled definition actually uses $(K_\calX+\lambda I)^{-1}$ on both sides of the propagated matrix, while the numerical restatement uses $(K_\calX^{-1}+\lambda I)^{-1}$ on the left. These matrices are generally different, so following the restatement computes a different estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The repeated numerical prescription would produce incorrect regularized coefficients if followed, although the earlier labeled definition and the formal regularized error analysis remain correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the left factor (K_X^{-1}+lambda I)^{-1} in the numerical restatement by (K_X+lambda I)^{-1}, so that both resolvent factors agree with eq:regularized_mcemdmd.
issues.why_classification: The old display explicitly claims to restate the cited labeled definition, which already fixes the correct factor, and the formal regularized analysis consistently uses that definition. The correction is uniquely forced by the old source and repairs only a copied formula, with no mathematical inference or guarantee requiring revision.

issues.title: Missing unit-ball condition in the Matérn total-error corollary

failure_location.quote: Then, for every $\veps > 0$  and all $f \in \bH$ with $\|f\|_\bH$, the full error admits the bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for every $\veps > 0$ and  for all $f \in \bH$, $\| f \|_\bH \leq 1$, we have the pointwise error bound

issues.failure_explanation: As printed, the corollary says only “with $\|f\|_\bH$” and supplies no admissibility condition, while its right-hand side is independent of f. Its proof merely invokes thm:total_error_bound, whose conclusion is for $\|f\|_\bH\leq1$. Thus the proof supports the unit-ball version, not the unrestricted or malformed statement; homogeneity also prevents such an f-independent estimate for arbitrary scalar multiples in general.
issues.overall_effect: The unregularized Matérn full-error corollary is overstated or mathematically incomplete as printed. No later formal result relies on the missing unrestricted version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Complete the malformed quantifier in cor:total_error_bound_matern as “all f in H with ||f||_H <= 1”; the bound and proof can then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The phrase ending with “with ||f||_H” is mathematically incomplete rather than a coherent unrestricted claim. The invoked general theorem, the parallel kernel results, and the f-independent right-hand side uniquely force the unit-ball normalization; unrestricted scalar multiples are impossible by homogeneity. Restoring the omitted comparison is therefore transcriptional.

issues.title: Wrong asymptotic direction in the kernel-eigenvalue amplification estimate
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that $\lambda_{\min}(K_\calX)=O(h_\calX^3)$, together with a factor bounded by $d/\lambda_{\min}(K_\calX)$, establishes an amplification of order $O(h_\calX^{-2})$. The old passage actually supplies only a one-sided upper bound on $\lambda_{\min}$. Such a bound permits a smaller eigenvalue—for example, $h^4$ is still $O(h^3)$—and therefore gives no upper bound on its reciprocal. A lower estimate $\lambda_{\min}\geq c h^3$ is the materially different input required.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed unregularized $O(h_\calX^{-2})$ amplification estimate is unsupported as printed. The later Tikhonov-based balancing calculation has its own $\sqrt{d/\lambda}$ argument and no formal theorem depends on this prose inference.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unsupported upper-order assertion by a justified lower spectral estimate. Introduce the separation distance q_X and apply the standard Wendland Gram-matrix bound lambda_min(K_X) >= c q_X^{2s-n}. For n=1, l=1, and s=2 this gives lambda_min(K_X) >= c q_X^3; for the equispaced design, q_X is comparable to h_X and d is comparable to h_X^{-1}, yielding sqrt(d/lambda_min(K_X))=O(h_X^{-2}).
issues.why_classification: The reciprocal estimate cannot follow from the printed upper bound, so reversing an asymptotic symbol without justification is inadequate. The same O(h_X^{-2}) claim can be recovered locally and without mathematical loss, but doing so requires a nontrivial quantitative kernel-matrix eigenvalue theorem and its specialization to the design geometry. This contained repair exceeds a routine minor correction while requiring no global reconstruction and affecting no dependent formal result.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Specifically, we have $\lambda_{\min}(\bbK_\calX) \geq C q_\calX^{2 s - n}$ with smoothness $s > n/2$ and dimension $n$ of the underlying kernel
